newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-SENNA TRIAL STARTS IN ITALY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SENNA TRIAL STARTS IN ITALY.

text.p: The trial of Formula One team chief Frank Williams and five others accused of manslaughter over the death of three times world champion Ayrton Senna started on Thursday.

The defendants, who include Williams' technical director Patrick Head and designer Adrian Newey, deny responsibility for the fatal crash at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix. The first session is due to focus on legal preliminaries.
Federico Bendinelli, managing director of the company running the Imola track at the time of the accident, was the only defendant present at the start of the trial.
The case has sent shock waves through Formula One. Teams have warned they will not risk competing in Italy in the event of a guilty verdict.
After Thursday's session, the trial is due to be adjourned until February 28. First witnesses are due to be heard next month and Frank Williams is not due to appear until April.

Senna suffered fatal head injuries when his Williams hurtled into a concrete wall at around 220 kph during the race on May 1, 1994. Italian state prosecutors believe that the steering column on the Brazilian's car snapped as a result of a poor weld.
